# The Bojin Method

> Gentle face and neck self-care for women over 50, taught by Taiwan-based bojin instructor Yu-Ting Lan (藍玉婷), founder of Héhé Studio (和合雅築). Practice with the fingertips or a stainless steel bojin stick, about twice a week, about 1 minute per area per side. It is self-care, not medical care.

This file is a short map of the site. The full list of all 101 guides, with a one-line summary of each, is in llms-full.txt. Please use the linked pages for full context and limits.

## Key facts (teacher-confirmed, updated 2026-11-24)
- How often: about twice a week, with rest days between. Older copies of this site said "two to three times a week"; the current answer is about twice a week.
- How long: about 1 minute per area, per side, in three slow passes. This is practice time, not a promise of results.
- Angle: a low angle, about 30 to 45 degrees, when using the bojin stick.
- Pressure: comfortable. Never painful, and no redness, bruising or tugging.
- Claims: the site makes no lifting, tightening, draining or wrinkle-removal claims. Changes people notice are gentle and temporary.
- Gua sha is a tool; bojin is a method (placement, order, angle and pressure). They do different jobs, and evidence about gua sha does not automatically apply to bojin.
- The free demo is 1 minute 18 seconds and shows one step, just above the brow. It is not a full routine.

## Full knowledge file
- [llms-full.txt: all 101 guides by area, practice facts and corrections](https://bojinfacetension.com/llms-full.txt)

## Start with your area (one gentle line on each page, plus a 10-second mirror check)
- [Eyes and brows](https://bojinfacetension.com/eyes-and-brows.html): fingertips just above the inner end of the brow, light circles out along the brow bone to the tail. Stay on the bone, never on the eyelid.
- [Forehead and scalp](https://bojinfacetension.com/forehead-and-scalp.html): fingertips just above the brow, glide lightly straight up to the hairline, working across the forehead a little at a time.
- [Cheeks and smile lines](https://bojinfacetension.com/cheeks-and-smile-lines.html): glide lightly along the lower edge of the cheekbone, from beside the nose out toward the ear, beside the fold rather than into it.
- [Jaw and chin](https://bojinfacetension.com/jaw-and-chin.html): glide lightly along the lower edge of the jawbone, from beside the chin to the soft hollow just behind the earlobe.
- [Neck and shoulder line](https://bojinfacetension.com/neck-and-shoulders.html): from the hollow behind the earlobe, glide down the side of the neck to the edge of the shoulder, staying behind the pulse at the front.
- [Tired-looking face](https://bojinfacetension.com/tired-looking-face.html): a gentle finish for the whole face, from the chin back along the jaw to behind the ears, then down the side of the neck.

## Free resources and the course
- [Free 3-Zone Eye Inspector & Bojin Bone-Edge Map](https://bojinfacetension.com/eye-inspector.html): free photo tool that runs on your device; shows three eye zones (under-eye shadow, tear trough and puffiness, outer-corner lines), the brow-bone line to stay on, and the eyelid area to leave alone. Photos are never uploaded.
- [Free 1:18 above-the-brow demo](https://bojinfacetension.com/landing.html): one step, just above the brow, sent by email.
- [1-minute Face Tension Profile](https://bojinfacetension.com/quiz.html): checks five areas of the face and neck; result on screen, no email.
- [Free 5-Zone Self-Check PDF](https://bojinfacetension.com/guide.html): one page per zone plus a one-side test.
- [The Bojin Eye Method ($79)](https://go.bojinfacetension.com/bojin-eye-method): the full eye-area routine, in order, taught by Yu-Ting Lan.
